data_quality_notes:
Research ran 06:32-07:09 ET (~37 min) and logged a RESEARCH COMPLETE block plus two addenda, so this is a full synthesis, not a salvage. Eight unique candidates were captured; seven are published and one (NKE) was moved to the watchlist rather than the recommendation list - see below.

REWARD-TO-RISK: all seven ratios were recomputed here from the final entry, target and downside rather than trusting the captured field. Spread: 2.27, 2.29, 2.51, 2.59, 2.68, 2.90, 3.21 against floors of 2.0 (swing) and 2.5 (long_term). Two of these - EVTC at 2.51 and CEG at 2.59 - sit close to the 2.5 long-term floor and deserve the scrutiny that implies, but the research log shows both targets were set from valuation anchors (EVTC 48 on a re-rating from 7.15x forward; CEG 385 on the prior high) before the ratio was measured, and the research phase's own audit caught and corrected two arithmetic errors in the conservative direction. This is not the clustered-just-above-the-floor signature that indicates fitted targets.

NKE IS ON THE WATCHLIST, NOT IN THE RECOMMENDATIONS, AND THIS IS AN EDITORIAL CALL. Research captured it deliberately at a 1.50 reward-to-risk against a 2.5 long-term floor, intending it as a downgrade notice for holders of the 08-17 and 08-18 positions and expecting enforcement to demote it. Publishing a failing ratio as a 'buy' row would misread to anyone who does not already own it, so it is carried as a watchlist entry with the full revised levels instead. The substance is unchanged: hold existing size, add nothing, target cut from 65/62 to 52, exit in full on a close below 38.60.

SINGLE POINT OF FAILURE - AUG 28. Three ideas (GLD 4%, EEM 2.5%, EVTC 2%) all require the dollar to keep falling. That is exactly at the correlation cap of 3, but it is also the three largest sizes in the report, and they die on the same morning if Kevin Warsh's first Jackson Hole keynote as Fed chair (Fri Aug 28) is hawkish and DXY bounces off its three-month low. Mitigation is built into the entries rather than asserted: GLD is wait:true with staged accumulation below spot, and EEM is explicitly half-size before the speech.

DIRECTION SKEW: 7 of 7 are long, in a tape that fell 0.87% on the discount rate. There is no short and no hedge. Research considered a short /MES and declined it for having no differentiated index view rather than manufacturing balance. The consequence for the reader is real: if the 30y keeps rising, essentially every idea here marks down together, and the fiscal-dominance thesis that makes gold work is the same one that de-rates equities.

HORIZON SKEW: 4 swing, 3 long_term, 0 intraday. Nothing intraday was manufactured - the equity session was closed throughout the run and the one intraday-grade dated event is seven days out.

TRACK-RECORD CAVEAT WORTH READING: the closed record is 0/3, all conviction 3, and both stop-outs (TJX, KRE) were 'buy the de-rated thing because the macro should help it'. DG, CEG and EVTC are structurally that same trade. At n=3 that is noise and the bar was not raised on it, but the mechanism is informative: in both losses the factor beta overwhelmed the idiosyncratic story. What differs today is that each of the three carries a company-specific confirmation the losers lacked - Bernstein traffic data, a net-positive insider tape, and a verified five-buyer insider cluster respectively.

PRICES: every last_price is the 2026-08-20 regular-session close, re-quoted at synthesis time and unchanged. Equities are pre-market, so a prior close is the freshest honest price, not a stale one. No price in this report is estimated.

SOURCES THAT FAILED. (1) Event contracts: market_data.py events returned count 0 for CPI, inflation, interest rates, Bitcoin, S&P 500, unemployment, recession and government shutdown; the only 'Fed' hit was a mis-indexed soccer parlay with null pricing. Robinhood Prediction Markets went unchecked today - a source failure, not a judgement that nothing was attractive. (2) Index and commodity quotes: SPX, NDX, DJI, RUT, VIX, DXY, gold, WTI, ES and NQ all failed (Yahoo HTTP 429 throughout, Finnhub index subscription required, stooq 404). Worked around with ETF proxies and sourced press figures; no index level here came from a failed fetch. There is no VIX reading at all, so nothing in this report is calibrated to implied volatility. (3) Robinhood's own futures-availability support page returned 404, so the venue check leaned on secondary sources - weaker evidence than wanted, though no futures idea is published today. (4) Third-party insider-cluster screeners disagreed with Finnhub Form 4 data on 3 of 5 names checked (VRCA and EDAP showed essentially no filings; ORN omitted five offsetting sales worth 5x the purchases). The one insider claim independently verified is EVTC's - 7 buys, 5 distinct buyers, $2.25M against $1.4M of sales - and it is why EVTC carries conviction 4.

NOT REACHED: ag/fertiliser, defence, REITs, Japan/Europe single names, and a systematic small-cap screen beyond the insider-cluster list. Crypto prices were fetched but no crypto candidate was taken, by choice, after the /MBTU6 short was closed.

STALE-CALENDAR WARNING: the earnings calendar was found to be wrong on one name (PRAX's PDUFA had moved from Sept 27 to Dec 27; only a direct search caught it). Any dated catalyst here that came from a calendar rather than a company filing should be treated as provisional. DG's Aug 27 date is confirmed from the company's own webcast announcement.

--- RED TEAM (phase 2c, 07:03-07:13 ET) ---

CUT 2, DOWNGRADED 1, FIXED LEVELS ON 3. Five of seven ideas survive.

Red team cut DHT (the entire crude-tanker thesis is unsourced - the two cited URLs are a generic market wrap and a precious-metals report, neither of which mentions tankers; and the 22.50 target sits 9.5% above the 52-week high of 20.55, so re-anchored to real resistance the trade gives 0.63:1 against a 2.0 floor) and cut BCC (its own counter_argument already concluded it should be closed, its only remaining argument was "it has not broken yet," and it closed 81.77 BELOW the 20-day at 81.99 that the thesis cites as intact - plus neither source concerns Boise Cascade or lumber). Both are open positions and both watchlist entries preserve the full management instruction rather than telling holders to dump.

Downgraded EVTC to conviction 3. Its conviction 4 rested on the insider cluster, and the Form 4s do not read the way the pitch claimed. The thesis stated "the stock still trades below where several of them bought" - that is FALSE: every disclosed purchase was struck between $23.37 and $26.42 (May 8 - Jun 12) against a $29.73 last price, so no insider paid today's price and a buyer here pays 13-27% more than all of them. The "$2.25M of buys against $1.4M of sales" framing also hid the ordering: the buys are May-June at $23-26, and the sales are Aug 11-14 at $29.50-$31.56 (Perez-Surillo $552k, Viglianco $836k, Polak $30k, all open-market code S), with the stock down 6.1% on that news around Aug 17. Insiders bought the lows and are selling the recovery. The valuation case (7.4x forward, 20% revenue growth, $150M buyback) is untouched and is why this is a downgrade rather than a cut.

LOOKBACK-WINDOW ERROR FOUND, AND IT IS SYSTEMATIC. The research phase pulled history with a 200-session window (~9.5 months) and then described the results as 52-week highs. Two ideas were affected. CEG: stated "-29.1% below its high" and anchored the 385 target to "the 384.98 prior high" - but 384.98 is the 200-session high; the true 52-week high is 412.70 and the real drawdown is -33.9%. The target is therefore conservative (7% below actual overhead) but the level was described wrongly and the de-rating understated. EVTC: the "34.41 prior high" in the scale plan is likewise the 200-session high; the 52-week high is 37.71. Both are corrected in place. GLD (509.70), DG (158.23), EEM (71.57) and BCC (91.97) were checked and their cited highs are genuine 52-week figures.

DG entry zone narrowed from 117.0-121.5 to 117.0-119.5 and size cut from 2.5% to 2.0%. The published 2.29 R:R holds only at the 119.00 ideal; a fill at the old 121.50 top of zone returned 1.42:1, below the 2.0 swing floor, so the zone as written permitted a fill that failed the report's own standard. At 119.50 the worst fill still returns 2.07:1. The size cut follows the idea's own admission that a guidance gap goes through the 112 stop rather than filling it - when the stop cannot be relied on, size is the only remaining control. The Bernstein store-visit claim WAS independently verified against the cited tradingpedia article (08-13), as were the Aug 27 8:00 CT/9:00 ET call and the Vasos/Lau hosts against the company webcast release; the March 2026 announcement that JJ Fleeman succeeds Vasos takes effect Jan 1, 2027 and does not touch this print.

GLD kept at conviction 4 - the numbers all reconcile (509.70 high, -18.53% off it, 200-day 413.21, 20-day 390.07, +14.9% off the 361.39 correction low, all refetched) and the entry is staged below spot, so this is not a crowded or extended entry. Two fixes rather than a downgrade. First, the 520 target implies roughly $5,600/oz and 557 implies ~$6,000, both ABOVE every forecast in the report's own evidence base (Goldman $4,900, HSBC $4,560, JPM $4,500); the R:R does not depend on them - anchored to the 509.70 prior high the trade still gives 2.94:1 against a 2.5 floor - so the scale plan now treats 509.70 as the evidenced level and 520/557 as aspiration. Second, the stated invalidation "central bank net purchases negative for two consecutive quarters" is unusable in any tradeable horizon because that series reports with a quarter or more of lag; the operative invalidation is the 361.39 close, 13.0% below spot.

THE SPREAD FAILURES ARE PRE-MARKET ARTIFACTS, NOT LIQUIDITY VERDICTS. validate_report.py failed EVTC (26.49%), BCC (24.04%) and DHT (6.22%) on bid/ask spread. Those quotes were pulled from Nasdaq at 4:00-7:00 ET and are placeholder pre-market books, not tradeable markets: BCC showed bid 66.76 / ask 85.00 at 4:00 ET on an $81.77 stock, EVTC bid 26.63 / ask 34.76 at 4:09 ET. All three trade with normal spreads in the regular session. Neither cut here was made on spread, and if the enforcement pass in phase 2d demotes EVTC on the same artifact the reader should understand that as a data problem, not a judgement that EVTC is untradeable. The two names quoted closest to the open - DG at 7:02 ET (1.48%) and CEG at 7:01 ET (0.57%) - show what the real books look like.

WHAT SURVIVES, AND WHAT IT STILL IS. Five ideas, 13.5% of capital, all long, no hedge, no short - the direction skew the synthesis phase flagged is unchanged and cutting two longs did not fix it. The dollar-down cluster (GLD 4%, EEM 2.5%, EVTC 2% = 8.5%) still dies together if Warsh's Jackson Hole debut on Fri Aug 28 is hawkish, and that is now 63% of the book's capital rather than 55%. One book-level contradiction the original report never stated and cutting BCC has now mostly resolved: GLD's thesis REQUIRES the long end to keep selling off, while BCC's key_risk named exactly that move as fatal - the report held both. A residual version survives in that CEG (capital-intensive, needs multiple expansion) and DG (consumer, discount-rate sensitive) are both hurt by the long-end move the top idea needs. Read GLD as the hedge against the other four rather than as an addition to them.

NOT RE-EXAMINED. EEM was left untouched - its 71.50 target is anchored to the genuine 71.57 52-week high, the half-size-before-Aug-28 staging is the correct mitigation, and its counter_argument already states the strongest objection (a real US term-premium shock historically takes EM down harder than the US, not less). The nine pre-existing watchlist entries and the NKE downgrade notice were not reviewed; the clock went to the top-ranked ideas as instructed.

market_context.summary:
The single fact that organises today: the Treasury more than doubled its long-bond buyback to at least $4B (effective Sep 9-Nov 4) and the long end sold off anyway - the 10y rose 4.7bp to 4.70% and the 30y rose 5.5bp to 5.249%, a two-decade high, the very next session. When the sovereign issuer's own bid cannot hold its own long end, and Bessent is simultaneously pressuring Warsh's Fed to ease, that is a fiscal-dominance signature rather than a policy-tightening one. The confirming tell is that the dollar fell with yields rising: DXY at 98.558, its lowest since May 14. Higher yields normally pull a currency up - yields up and currency down means investors are demanding more compensation to hold the debt and leaving the currency anyway.

That one fact explains three tapes that otherwise look unrelated. Equities de-rated on the discount rate (S&P -0.87% to 7,641.16, Nasdaq -1.0%, Dow -1.32%, small caps worst at -1.34%); gold held bid; and bitcoin ran roughly $64k to $77.9k in three sessions, +8.3% on the day, with over $1B of shorts liquidated in a single hour through $69k.

The second driver is the US consumer cracking. Walmart fell 9% on 2.6% same-store sales, with management explicitly blaming $4 gasoline for a psychological hit to spending. That is one trade, not two: $4 gas is simultaneously the bull case for energy and the bear case for discretionary retail, and XLE closed green on a red tape. The next fortnight is a consumer referendum - nearly every dated earnings event through Sep 2 is a retailer - which argues for expressing the consumer view where trade-down helps rather than where it hurts.

The dated event that matters most is not an earnings print. Kevin Warsh delivers his first Jackson Hole keynote as Fed chair on the morning of Fri Aug 28, 19 days before the Sep 16 FOMC, with no track record as this speaker to price against. It sits on top of the dollar, the long end and gold at once, and it is why the dollar-sensitive entries in this report are staged or explicitly half-size rather than full positions today.

The actual 52-week high is 412.70, so 385 sits ~7% below real overhead resistance. catalyst.event: US grid scarcity repricing: PJM capacity cleared at $329.17/MW-day for 2026/27 versus $28.92 for 2024/25, and the 2027/28 auction failed to procure enough supply for the first time in PJM history. PJM plans a reliability backstop procurement auction in Autumn 2026.
catalyst.action: Accumulate in thirds on weakness over the next two quarters. The driver runs to 2030; there is no reason to pay up for a single entry.

recommendations.thesis: The physical fact and the share price are pointing in opposite directions, which is the whole idea. PJM capacity prices went from $28.92 to $329.17 per MW-day in two delivery years - more than tenfold - and the 2027/28 auction failed to secure enough supply for the first time ever, with data centers set to add over 30GW of peak demand by 2030. Constellation owns the nuclear baseload that hyperscalers specifically need for 24/7 carbon-free power, yet it trades 33.9% below its 52-week high of 412.70, having been de-rated on political headlines rather than on power economics. One director bought $417,931 on the open market and there have been zero insider sales in six months.
recommendations.key_risk: The de-rating is not irrational and the political risk is concrete, not hypothetical: the Trump Administration and mid-Atlantic governors have floated capping electricity rates in exactly the region where these assets sit, and New York has a one-year moratorium on environmental permits for large data centers. A rate cap converts a scarcity windfall into a regulated return and would break this thesis outright. Management also guided 2026 adjusted earnings below consensus and is still digesting the Calpine acquisition, so the earnings bridge to a 385 share price is not yet visible. Invalidation: mid-Atlantic rate caps being enacted in law, or PJM capacity clearing materially lower in the Autumn 2026 backstop auction.
recommendations.counter_argument: The market has seen the same PJM numbers I have and sold the stock anyway, which is usually a sign the constraint is not the scarcity but who is allowed to collect on it. Political backlash tends to arrive precisely when a windfall becomes large and visible enough to be worth legislating against - so the very datapoint I am calling the bull case ($329/MW-day) is what makes a rate cap likely. Red team adds: the drawdown is deeper than the write-up stated - 33.9% off 412.70, not 29.1% - so the argument that the de-rating is finished is weaker, not stronger, than it was presented. The stock hit a 52-week low and drew a Citi downgrade; buying an AI-power darling that has already lost 35% of its value in the first half on the argument that it is cheap assumes the de-rating is over, and nothing in the tape says that yet. Note also that the PJM auction results are a year old and among the most written-up datapoints in US power - the scarcity is not the differentiated part of this idea; the willingness to underwrite the political risk is.
